name: The Screen-Size Checker
oneLiner: Captures every screen at nine viewport profiles via Playwright device emulation and reports capture coverage as a pass/fail grid plus a single percentage.
lead: Emulates nine viewport profiles — a 1920×1080 desktop plus four phones in portrait and landscape — captures each mapped screen at each, then checks the captures dir for the expected PNG per screen-per-viewport. Output is a grid (screens × viewports) with a mark where a capture exists and a dash where it's missing, plus an overall coverage percentage. A missing cell means the screen failed to render at that viewport.
chore: By hand: open the browser device toolbar, pick a profile, reload, navigate to a screen, screenshot, repeat per profile and per screen. Nine profiles × dozens of screens is hundreds of manual captures — tedious, slow, and non-deterministic across testers.
instead: One run captures every screen at every viewport and emits a coverage grid — mark where the capture landed, dash where it didn't — with total coverage as a single percentage.
whyItMatters: A dash in the grid is an early signal that a screen breaks at that viewport — caught before a user on that exact device hits it.

howItWorks.step: Selects the viewport set — the full run is nine profiles (desktop + four phones, portrait and landscape); a quick run drops the landscape profiles.
howItWorks.explain: Static profile list filtered by one flag. Each entry pins an explicit `width`×`height` **and** a Playwright `project` name — the `project` is what actually applies device emulation, while the width/height are what the grid labels. `includeLandscape` true returns all nine; false filters out `type === 'landscape'`, leaving desktop plus the upright phones — the common-case sweep that skips the slower sideways captures. The `type` tag, not the dimensions, is the filter key, so adding a new portrait phone needs no change here.

howItWorks.step: Runs one Playwright project per viewport — Chromium for desktop/Android profiles, WebKit for iPhone profiles — capturing every mapped screen at that emulated device.
howItWorks.explain: Builds the `playwright test` argv by expanding the selected viewports into one **`--project=` flag each** — the project name is the hook into `responsive.config.ts`, which binds it to a device profile and its engine (**Chromium** for desktop/Android, **WebKit** for iPhone, so iOS rendering matches the real Safari engine). `--grep @design-capture` restricts the run to the tagged capture spec, keeping the rest of the suite out. It runs with `stdio: 'inherit'` so Playwright's progress streams live, under a **600s** ceiling. As with the sibling agents, a **non-zero exit is expected** — some screens legitimately fail to capture — so it is logged `warn`, and the missing PNGs are inferred by the existence check downstream rather than treated as a hard error.

howItWorks.step: For each screen × viewport, checks the captures dir for the expected `<screenId>-<viewport>.png` and tallies existing vs missing.
howItWorks.explain: Walks the full **screen × viewport matrix** and, for each cell, reconstructs the expected filename via `VIEWPORT_LABEL_MAP[vp.project]` — the map converts the Playwright project name into the same slug the capture spec used to write the PNG, so a mismatch here would silently read every cell as missing. `fs.existsSync` **is** the pass/fail test: no image comparison, just presence, because a screen that crashed at a viewport simply never produces its file. It rolls up `capturedViewports` per screen and the run-wide `totalCaptures` (`screens × viewports`, the denominator) and `capturedCount` (the numerator) that yield the single coverage percentage.

howItWorks.step: Renders the coverage grid — screens down the rows, viewports across the header, `Y`/`-` per cell — plus a 'Missing Captures' list naming every incomplete screen and its missing viewports.
howItWorks.explain: Renders two views of the same data. The grid uses **only the first token** of each viewport label (`label.split(' ')[0]`) as its column header to keep the table narrow, then emits one row per screen with `Y`/`-` cells in the **same order** as the header — the alignment is positional, so the header and cell arrays must iterate the same `viewports`. The second pass filters to screens where `capturedViewports < totalViewports` and lists each one's failed viewports **by name** under `Missing Captures`, turning the grid's dashes into an actionable checklist. When no screen is incomplete, that section is omitted entirely rather than printed empty.

howItWorks.step: Serializes the report to JSON and Markdown, and with `--word` emits a `.docx` laying out each screen's captures side by side per viewport.
howItWorks.explain: Derives one timestamp — ISO with `:` and `.` replaced by `-` and sliced to `yyyy-mm-ddThh-mm-ss` so it's **filesystem-safe, lexically sortable, and unique** — and reuses it across all sibling outputs so the `.json`, `.md`, and optional `.docx` from one run share a suffix. JSON is always written pretty-printed at **2-space** indent (diff-friendly); the Markdown is the rendered grid. The `.docx` is the only conditional branch, gated on `generateWord`: it awaits `generateWordDoc`, which **embeds the actual PNGs** rather than linking them, and only then is its path added to the returned map — so callers can tell which artifacts actually exist.

examples.caption: Full sweep across all nine viewports
examples.input: 25 screens requested at every viewport profile.
examples.output: A 25 × 9 grid, an '88% coverage' headline, and a 'Missing Captures' list naming the three screens that failed to render at the smallest phone viewport.

examples.caption: Sign-in flow, portrait only
examples.input: Run scoped to the login and welcome screens, landscape profiles excluded.
examples.output: A compact grid showing both screens captured at desktop and every portrait phone viewport, coverage 100%.

examples.caption: Screen that fails to render in landscape
examples.output: Grid marks the screen captured in portrait but a dash in landscape, listing that screen+viewport under 'Missing Captures' for follow-up.

underHood.heading: Selecting viewport profiles
underHood.output: Either five (desktop + portrait phones) or all nine explicit width×height profiles.

underHood.heading: Capturing every screen per viewport
underHood.input: The mapped screen list plus the selected profiles.
underHood.output: Playwright screenshots using two engines to match real devices — Chromium for desktop/Android, WebKit (Safari's engine) for iPhone profiles.

underHood.heading: Checking capture existence
underHood.output: A captured/missing flag per cell of the matrix.

underHood.heading: Building the coverage grid
underHood.output: A `Y`/`-` grid, an overall coverage percentage, and an explicit missing-captures list.

underHood.heading: Writing the report
underHood.whenRuns: Last, once the grid is built.
underHood.input: The finished grid and its totals.
underHood.output: A JSON file, a Markdown report, and — with `--word` — a `.docx` with the PNGs embedded.

prerequisites: Node ≥ 18 and a terminal (macOS/Linux shell or Windows PowerShell).
The target app running at a reachable URL (dev or QA) — the agent captures it live at each viewport.
~10 min on first run: `npx playwright install` downloads the Chromium and WebKit engines before any capture.
The screen list and per-screen navigation already wired into the agent (no per-run setup for this part).

steps.label: Install Node.js — the runtime for the agent.
steps.cmd:
# macOS (with Homebrew):
brew install node

# or download the LTS installer from nodejs.org, then check it worked:
node -v   # should print v18 or higher
steps.why: The agent is a TypeScript program executed by Node. One-time install per machine.
steps.firstRun: Only needed once per new machine.

steps.label: Install dependencies — once for the agent, once for the Playwright package it drives.
steps.cmd:
cd path/to/the-agents
npm install

cd Playwright
npm install
npx playwright install   # downloads the actual Chromium + WebKit browser engines
steps.why: The agent lives in the project root; the capture layer lives in a sibling `Playwright` dir with its own deps. `npx playwright install` fetches the engines — Chromium for desktop/Android, WebKit for iPhone — not bundled with the npm package.
steps.firstRun: Downloads deps plus the browser engines — the slow part (5-10 min).
steps.rerun: No-op once installed, unless a dependency or browser version changed.

steps.label: Set the target URL.
steps.why: `APP_URL` is the live app opened at each viewport. Unset, it falls back to a built-in default that won't be your app.

steps.label: Run it.
steps.why: The full run: captures every mapped screen at nine viewports (desktop + four phones, portrait and landscape) and writes the coverage grid. `--word` additionally emits a `.docx` with the captures embedded.
steps.firstRun: Captures every screen at every viewport from scratch.
steps.rerun: `--capture-only` refreshes captures only; `--report-only` rebuilds the grid from on-disk captures without re-capturing.

steps.label: Open the generated report.
steps.why: The `.md` holds the coverage grid — `Y` per captured screen × viewport cell, `-` per gap — plus the explicit missing-captures list.

inputs.name: APP_URL (environment variable)
inputs.desc: URL of the running app to capture.

inputs.name: --screens <list>
inputs.desc: Comma-separated screen ids to scope the run to a subset instead of the full set.

inputs.name: --landscape, --capture-only, --report-only, --headed, --word
inputs.desc: Flags to add landscape viewports, split capture/report phases, run headed (visible browser), or emit a `.docx`.

outputs.name: responsive-report-<timestamp>.json / .md
outputs.desc: Machine-readable and rendered coverage grid plus the overall percentage.

outputs.name: responsive-report-<timestamp>.docx (optional)
outputs.desc: `.docx` with the captures embedded; emitted only with `--word`.

outputs.name: outputs/mobile/captures/*.png
outputs.desc: Raw captures, one per screen per viewport — reused by `--report-only` on a later run.

runbook.rerun: `--report-only` skips capture and rebuilds the grid from existing captures — useful to re-derive the numbers without a re-capture. A flagless run always re-captures every screen at every viewport, since coverage shifts with every build.
runbook.integrate: Run the nine-viewport sweep as a pre-release build gate; a dropping coverage percentage, or a screen gaining a new `-` in the grid, is a regression worth blocking on.

video.caption: 2-3 min screen recording: watch the agent capture every screen at nine viewport profiles and build the coverage grid.
script: Open a terminal beside the app so viewers can see it load at different sizes.
Say: 'This agent photographs every screen at nine different screen sizes and tells you how much of it survived the shrink.'
Run `node -v` to confirm Node is installed; say one line about what Node is.
Run `npm install` in the project root and in the Playwright folder (or note it's already done); mention `npx playwright install` downloads the actual browser engines it drives.
Show the one `export APP_URL=...` line; say 'this is the only place the app's address lives.'
Run `npm run responsive:test -- --word`; narrate as it steps through desktop, then each phone size, upright and sideways.
Open the produced `.md` report; point at the tick/dash grid and the overall coverage percentage.
Scroll to the 'Missing Captures' section and read out one screen that didn't survive a particular size.
Close: 'A dash in this grid is the early warning — long before a customer on that exact phone complains.'
